title: Recording, mixing: Little Woman Love, Love Is Strange, Bip Bop Link by Wings | 1971
content:
Studio Two, EMI Studios, Abbey Road
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineers: Tony Clark, Alan Parsons

The newly-named Wings were mostly dormant during September 1971, not least due to the birth of Stella McCartney on the 13th. They resumed recording on 2 October at Abbey Road.

The first song to be tackled was an outtake from the Ram sessions. ‘Little Woman Love’ had been started in New York in November 1970, and Paul McCartney was considering releasing it as a single. He added more guitar parts during this session, before he, Linda McCartney, and Denny Laine overdubbed vocals.

The rest of the morning was taken up with mixing ‘Little Woman Love’ and ‘Half Past Ten’. The latter had been recorded on 24 July 1971, but McCartney had noted its similarity to ‘Love Is Strange’, a 1956 R&B hit. After the mix was completed, he decided to turn it into a cover version with later overdubs.

In the afternoon he added lead guitar to ‘Wild Life’, then recorded a new intro with vocals and acoustic guitar.

While studio engineer Tony Clark was preparing the microphones for the recording, McCartney played a piece of fingerpicked guitar music. This was captured on tape, and was released as ‘Bip Bop Link’ on Wild Life.

I do remember when Paul was playing it, and I was mic’ing it up; I just used a couple of mics. And I thought crikey, what a fine musician he is. Because that’s quite a complex piece of musicianship. It’s just him and an acoustic guitar. That’s not easy, and he played it fantastic.
Tony Clark, 23 March 2017
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 1: 1969-73, Allan Kozinn, Adrian Sinclair
Page last updated: 19 November 2025
